For Respondents No.1 to 3 : Mr. Ajit Sharma, Deputy Advocate General.
For Respondent No.4 : Ms. Madhurika Sekhon, Advocate.
Rakesh Kainthla, Judge

The petitioner has filed the present petition for quashing of Fir No. 01 of
2022, dated 10.01.2022 registered for the commission of offences punishable under Sections 498A,
354, 406 and 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as Ipc) at
Women Police Station Nahan, Whether reporters of Local Papers may be allowed to see the
judgment?

Yes. 
2024:Hhc:9474 District Sirmaur, H.P. and the consequential proceedings arising out of the Fir.
2.  It has been asserted that the matter has arisen out of a marital discord.
It has been compromised between the parties and the parties do not want to proceed further with the matter after the settlement.

The statement of the informant-Promilla Devi was recorded on 05.09.2024, in which she stated that the parties had divorced each other and as per the settlement between the parties,
she did not want to proceed further.
3. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the records carefully.
4. Since the matter had arisen out of the marital discord which has been settled by the compromise between the parties, therefore, the FIR can be quashed based on the compromise.

The Courts have already quashed the F.I.R. registered for the commission of an offence punishable under Section 498-A of IPC in Gian Singh versus State, 2012 (10) SCC 303, Narender versus State of Punjab, 2014 (16) SCC 466, Vikas Singh vs. State of H.P. (2023)I DMC 335 (HP) and Sanjay Kumar vs. State of H.P 2023 (1) 2024:HHC:9474 Him L.R. 602 based on the compromise.
